sections.h2: What is the City of Fairfax, and how is it different from Fairfax County?
sections.html:
The City of Fairfax is a small independent city of about 6.3 square miles in Northern Virginia, 14 miles west of Washington, D.C., and it is separate from Fairfax County even though it is the county seat. Most of the county surrounds it, and a small piece of the county, including the courthouse complex and the jail, is an exclave inside the city limits.

That difference matters when you sell. A house with a Fairfax mailing address might be inside the city or in the county, and the two bill taxes, assess property and run schools through different offices. Check your tax bill to see who sends it.

The Census Bureau counted 24,146 residents in 2020 and estimates 26,772 for 2025, an increase of about 10.9 percent. The 2020 census found 9,330 housing units, with 5.7 percent vacant.

sections.h2: How did Fairfax become a city?
sections.html:
Fairfax started as the Town of Providence, created by the legislature in 1805, and it grew around the county courthouse. The name changed to Fairfax, the town incorporated in 1874, and a court order made it an independent city in 1961. The present charter dates to 1966.

The Battle of Fairfax Court House on June 1, 1861, was the first land battle of the Civil War, and a second fight took place there on June 27, 1863. The former county courthouse is the oldest historic building in the city, and the City of Fairfax Historic District was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1987.

If your house is in or near the old town, check whether any exterior work you did needs city approval before you list it. The planning office can answer that.

A homeowner vacancy rate of 0.7 percent means few owned houses sit empty. A vacant or neglected house in the city stands out to neighbors and to code staff, so owners who are not living in a house often decide to sell it quickly.

sections.h2: Who employs people in Fairfax city?
sections.html:
The City of Fairfax government is the largest single employer inside the city limits, with 600 employees in the city's 2025 annual financial report. The report lists the next employers in ranges:

  • Sentry Force, Zeta Associates and Ted Britt Ford, each with 250 to 499 employees.
  • Premium Home Health Care, Fairfax Operator, Community Systems, Trident Systems and Home Depot, each with 100 to 249.
  • Several car dealerships and home care companies also appear, including Farrish of Fairfax and Ourisman Fairfax Toyota.

George Mason University, the largest university in Virginia by head count with 33,917 students, sits just south of the city limits, with a small part of its grounds inside the city. Many residents work at the university, in Tysons or in Washington. Owners who are moving for a new assignment may need to sell on short notice, and a cash sale can be scheduled around a move.

sections.h2: How does Fairfax city assess real estate?
sections.html:
The City of Fairfax assesses every property each year at 100 percent of fair market value, effective January 1. The city says the assessor does not set the tax rate. The City Council sets the rate during the budget process, and the rate times your assessment gives your tax bill.

For residential property the assessor prefers the market data approach, comparing recent sales of similar houses in the same neighborhood. The city's assessment calendar looks like this:

DateStep
January 1Effective date of assessment
February 202026 assessment notices mailed
April 3Deadline to request an administrative review
Mid MayReal estate tax bills mailed
June 30Deadline to appeal to the Board of Equalization

The city's assessments page also states that city taxes are paid on June 21 and December 5, and gives the Treasurer's number as 703-385-7900. It says the city offers tax relief for the elderly and disabled.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Fairfax city assessment?
sections.html:
You start with the Real Estate Assessment Office at City Hall, and if that does not resolve it, you appeal to the Board of Equalization. The city tells owners they have 30 days after notices go out to request a review by phone or in person, and an appraiser can go over the data and schedule an inspection.

The Board of Equalization has three members, appointed by the Circuit Court and drawn from city property owners. It can affirm, reduce or raise an assessment to equalize the tax burden. If you disagree with the board, you can go to Circuit Court.

  • Gather recent comparable sales and photographs of condition problems.
  • Fill out the city's administrative appeal form before the April 3 deadline.
  • Keep copies of repair estimates if you believe the assessor overlooked damage.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit affect selling a house in Fairfax city?
sections.html:
Fairfax city has strong road access, and buyers know it. U.S. 50 and U.S. 29 meet in the northeast corner and run together as Fairfax Boulevard for about 2.8 miles through the city. State Routes 123, 236 and 237 also pass through, and Interstate 66 runs just outside the limits, reached by way of U.S. 50 or Route 123.

Rail service is outside the city. The Vienna station on the Washington Metro Orange Line and the Burke Centre station for Virginia Railway Express and Amtrak serve trips to and from Fairfax, and the city runs its own CUE Bus. Work on Blenheim Boulevard began in July 2026 and is scheduled to finish in July 2028, so owners on or near that road may see construction while their house is on the market.

sections.h2: What costs come with a Fairfax sale, and what is a cash sale like?
sections.html:
A Fairfax seller pays any unpaid city real estate tax out of the sale proceeds, plus Virginia's grantor tax. Virginia law gives tax liens priority over other liens, and the state statute says tax liability between buyer and seller is prorated by contract. The grantor tax is 50 cents for each $500 of the price, normally paid by the seller. Deeds are recorded with the land records office at the Fairfax County Judicial Center.

A cash sale skips the listing steps, repairs and showings. We can buy directly or bring a vetted cash buyer, and the offer depends on the house's condition and title. If you want to compare it with a listing, ask for the offer first and decide afterward.

faqs.q: Is the City of Fairfax the same as Fairfax County?
faqs.a: No. The City of Fairfax is an independent city that sits inside the county but runs its own government, assessments and tax billing. It remains the county seat.

faqs.q: When are City of Fairfax real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: The city's assessments page says taxes are paid on June 21 and December 5. Call the Treasurer at 703-385-7900 to confirm your current bill and any amount due before closing.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Fairfax city assessment?
faqs.a: For 2026, the administrative review request was due April 3, and an appeal to the Board of Equalization was due June 30. Dates shift each year, so check the assessments page.

faqs.q: Does the seller pay a tax when a Virginia house sells?
faqs.a: Yes, Virginia charges a grantor tax of 50 cents per $500 of the sale price, and the seller usually pays it. The contract can assign it differently.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Fairfax house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase the house in its current condition, and you choose the closing date. A title company still handles the deed and any payoffs.

faqs.q: Which schools serve the City of Fairfax?
faqs.a: The city's public schools include Fairfax High School, Katherine Johnson Middle School, Daniels Run Elementary and Providence Elementary. They are owned by the city and run by Fairfax County Public Schools under a contract.
